USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the mid-September deputy talks and the early-October Lighthizer–Mnuchin–Liu He round without adding new tariffs or rolling back existing ones. Keep List 3 at 25%, List 4A at 15%, Huawei on the Entity List, and the delayed 25-to-30 percent hike as unused leverage past October 15 only if Beijing puts enforceable IP/tech-transfer text and verified farm purchases on the table. Do not lock in purchase-only or partial-rollback commitments before that matching offer is real.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderately elevated, not existential. Combined Section 301 coverage now includes List 3 at 25% and List 4A at 15% on roughly $110–125B, with China’s ~$75B retaliation (including autos) in force since September 1, so US farm and auto-export constituencies remain exposed. August ISM manufacturing fell to 49.1 — first contraction in three years — with new export orders at their weakest since 2009; Michigan sentiment dropped to 89.8 in August before a partial rebound to 93.2; the 10-year yield sank to 1.47% in early September (latest 1.80%) and funds rate was cut to 2.04%; VIX spiked to 24.59 on August 5 after the List 4/CNY-7/manipulator sequence. Moody’s has already put the tariff drag near 0.3% of GDP and ~300k fewer jobs. That is material GDP and sector pain, not a clean leverage opportunity. It is also not +0.5-level high threat: industrial production is roughly flat, the goods deficit narrowed to −$69.5B, VIX is back to 13.95, and China is blinking on agriculture — a 16-category exemption list on September 11 plus soybean/pork exclusions and reported cargo inquiries on September 13. Action should stay at hold/negotiate because a further hike (the unused 25→30% on $250B, or more Entity-List expansion) is likely to be met with more CNY weakness and farm retaliation, repeating the August shock just as consumer List 4B (phones, laptops, toys) looms on December 15. Unilateral concession or purchase-only deals would also be premature: May talks collapsed when China tried to reopen structural text, and Lighthizer is still seeking a “real agreement” on IP and forced tech transfer, not an interim goods swap. Use the goodwill window to test whether Beijing will put enforcement language and verified purchases on paper; if not, existing tariffs already supply pressure without a new escalation.
key_factors: List 3 at 25% plus List 4A at 15% already in force; unused 25-to-30% hike delayed only to Oct 15
China retaliation on ~$75B including autos, offset by Sept 11/13 farm and industrial exemptions
US manufacturing contraction (ISM 49.1) and farm-belt exposure versus still-stable IP and calmer VIX
Huawei Entity List and currency-manipulator designation remain open non-tariff fronts
Deputy talks now, Liu He round in early October; structural IP/enforcement still unresolved after the May collapse

Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).

Trump tweets that negotiations are going "too slowly" and that China is attempting to "renegotiate."
Michigan consumer sentiment fell from 97.2 (Apr) to 89.8 (Aug), then 93.2 (Sep).
10-year Treasury yield 1.80% on 2019-09-18, down 63 bp in the window; trough 1.47% on Sept 3.

Deputy-level talks in Washington paving the way for October high-level meetings; Lighthizer seeking a real IP/tech-transfer agreement, some movement on ag purchases.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the working-level meetings this week and the October Liu He–Lighthizer/Mnuchin round without new tariff hikes or entity-list escalation, and without locking in large purchase or structural commitments. Keep the limited farm and industrial exemptions already announced—they serve our own pork-shortage and input needs as well as signaling goodwill—and use talks to test whether Washington will delay the October 15 rate hike and December 15 List 4B in exchange for calibrated agricultural buying. Do not reopen May-style legal-code/enforcement concessions unless the US puts live tariffs on the table.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. List 3 has been at 25% since 10 May and List 4A took effect at 15% on 1 September, so a large share of our US-bound exports is already taxed; Huawei and affiliates remain on the Entity List with Google/Android and US chip supply cut off (15–16 May), which hits the national tech-champion and self-sufficiency agenda. CNY broke 7 in early August, Treasury labeled us a currency manipulator (5 Aug), and the yuan was still ~7.08 on 18 September. August industrial output rose only 4.4% YoY—the weakest single month since 2002 aside from early-2009—and merchandise imports are down ~7.4% over the 180-day window, so the dispute is biting the real economy and export hubs. That maps near the +0.5 CHN anchor (major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level Huawei targeting). It is not +1.0: reserves are stable near $3.11T, seasonally adjusted exports have not collapsed, and Huawei has continued to ship. The action should not match the threat with further escalation. A second-round hike after 23 August already produced Trump’s “find an alternative to China” order and a List 4 rate lift to 15%; another move could bring the delayed 25%→30% step on ~$250B (now slated 15 Oct) and List 4B on phones/laptops (15 Dec). Both sides have already started a thaw: our 11 September 16-category exemption list, 13 September soybean/pork exclusion and resumed bean buying, and Trump’s delay of the 1 October hike past the 70th-anniversary holiday. Working-level talks are set for this week and Liu He for early October; Trump has said he would “consider” an interim deal. That is a negotiate window, not a concede-purchases or full-rollback moment—there is still no locked matching US offer, and a broad structural package failed in May. Limited farm buying is cheap because African swine fever and food CPI (index 107.8→109.8) give us an independent reason to import pork and soy.
key_factors: List 3 at 25% plus List 4A at 15% already live; List 4B (phones/laptops) still set for 15 Dec
Huawei Entity List remains the core tech/self-sufficiency threat
August industrial output 4.4% YoY and falling imports show the war is hitting the real economy
CNY above 7 and US currency-manipulator designation add FX/financial stigma
Mid-September mutual goodwill (China farm/industrial exemptions; US delay of the 1 Oct hike to 15 Oct) and talks scheduled this week and early October
Pork/ASF inflation makes limited US farm purchases domestically useful, not just a concession
Further escalation risks the Oct 15 25-to-30% step and Dec 15 consumer-electronics tariffs; large structural concessions without tariff rollback would repeat the May breakdown

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods... Trump orders US companies to "immediately start looking for an alternative to China" and directs a 5-point increase on the planned List 4 rate (to 15%).
China industrial production index (same period previous year=100): 104.4 in August 2019 (i.e., +4.4% YoY), after 104.8 in July and 106.3 in June.
CNY/USD 7.0849 on 2019-09-18, up from ~6.71 in late March; broke 7.0 on 2019-08-05.
China merchandise imports down about 7.4% over the window, latest $167.7B (Sept) vs $181.1B (April).
China CPI index rose from 107.8 (April) to 109.8 (September), consistent with food-price pressure.
Industrial output rose 4.4 percent from a year earlier... the lowest single-month figure since 2002, with only a combined Jan-Feb result in 2009 dipping lower.

Working-level discussions... next week in Washington. Assuming they go well, Chinese Vice Premier Liu He is scheduled to meet with Lighthizer and Mnuchin in Washington during the first half of October.

China will exclude imports of U.S. soybeans, pork and other farm goods from additional trade war tariffs... in response to the U.S. decision to postpone an increase in the tariff rate on $250 billion of Chinese goods from October 1 to October 15.
